title: Exact chiral symmetry with quantum signal processing
authors: Henry Lamm, Alessandro Roggero, Hersh Singh, Luca Spagnoli
abstract: We give a quantum signal processing (QSP) algorithm for the overlap fermion Hamiltonian which preserves the Ginsparg-Wilson relation up to a controllable error $ε_e$. Quantum simulations of Dirac fermions with exact chiral symmetry are thus nearly free: applying the overlap Hamiltonian costs only a factor logarithmic in $ε_e$ more than the Wilson-Dirac Hamiltonian. Comparing to domain-wall fermions, a mild overhead is found in circuit complexity while reducing qubit costs. We show how QSP effectively constructs an extra dimension when simulating the overlap operator, illustrating that the scaling of quantum algorithms reflects the deeper physics of overlap fermions arising at the boundary of domain-wall fermions.
summary: This paper presents a Quantum Signal Processing algorithm to simulate lattice fermions with exact chiral symmetry, specifically targeting the Overlap fermion Hamiltonian. By using QSP, they achieve an efficient simulation that only incurs a logarithmic overhead compared to simpler methods while rigorously controlling the resulting violation of chiral symmetry ($\propto \epsilon_e$). This work advances quantum simulation techniques for fundamental problems in particle physics.
main_problem: Developing efficient quantum algorithms for simulating lattice fermions while rigorously preserving exact chiral symmetry.
main_result: A Quantum Signal Processing (QSP) algorithm can simulate the overlap fermion Hamiltonian with only a logarithmic overhead compared to the Wilson-Dirac case, maintaining chiral symmetry up to a controllable error $\epsilon_e$.
method: The authors employ QSP techniques combined with block encoding to approximate the sign function required for the Overlap operator, allowing time evolution simulation on quantum hardware.
model_or_system: The study focuses on simulating lattice Quantum Chromodynamics (QCD) using Dirac fermions. It compares three formulations: Wilson-Dirac, Domain-Wall, and Overlap fermions, all defined by specific Hamiltonians ($\hat{h}_w$, $\hat{h}_{ov}$).
key_observables: Chiral symmetry violation quantified by the commutator $[\hat{\gamma}_5, \hat{h}]$, and the computational cost scaling (memory/gate count).
important_parameters: The approximation error ($\epsilon_e$), the lattice size ($N$), and the parameter $\kappa$ related to eigenvalue bounds.
main_assumptions: The primary assumption is that the sign function can be accurately approximated by a polynomial of degree $M$, leading to an error bound proportional to $\epsilon_e$.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from defining the physical problem (lattice fermions) and comparing Hamiltonians, to detailing the QSP implementation for the Overlap operator, and finally deriving rigorous bounds on chiral symmetry violation based on the approximation error.
why_interesting: While focused on high-energy physics, the core methodology—using QSP to implement complex non-local operators (like the sign function) while controlling systematic errors ($\epsilon_e$) in a quantum simulation framework—is highly relevant for developing fault-tolerant algorithms for general many-body Hamiltonians.
